account:
Something unusually large and coordinated is being arranged for eighteen hundred today in the town hall's great hall. The neighbour reported 201 fresh loaves in the hall chest, all baked yesterday, and said, 'We made it!' and that working together had been a pleasure. I have not personally counted that bread. The innkeeper says he requested it for committee hospitality, identifies the hospitality committee as himself, builder and freight, and asks that the bread remain reserved. He repeatedly asks me to arrive at eighteen, not early, and says everything will be discussed then. Freight has just asked to speak with him outside about today's arrangements.

The secretary has supplied no agenda or preparatory correspondence and says none was provided. She will escort me to the evening meeting. She has confirmed coordination but not its purpose; I have authorized no bread purchase. The neighbour was involved in the baking effort but has also asked who the gathering is for, so she may not know the full plan either. Some earlier conversations were too far away for me to understand; I cannot treat those as evidence of what was said.

My best guess is that this is a planned communal gathering, perhaps a surprise celebration or hospitality event involving many townspeople. The quantity of bread and insistence that I not arrive early suggest preparation they wish to keep out of my view, but I do not know the occasion and have no evidence of wrongdoing. I am curious rather than certain that anything sinister is happening. I intend to keep my ordinary appointments: office correspondence now, mill inspection at ten, lunch at home, council letters at thirteen, tea at the neighbour's cottage at fifteen, office at sixteen thirty, and the hall meeting at eighteen.
